coordination.oneSessionPerLane: Each of the ten chats must choose exactly one L01-L10 ID, write a unique sessionId claim into its lane through a fresh-main optimistic commit, and verify no other unexpired claim occupies it. Do not work an already claimed lane without an explicit same-user handoff.
coordination.claimContract: claim = null or {sessionId, holder, claimedAt, expiresAt}; expiresAt is ISO timestamp. Expiry only permits a deliberate fresh-head reclaim and never authorizes clobbering an in-flight commit. Claims are advisory coordination plus optimistic SHA conflict detection, NOT an OS/distributed lock.
coordination.writeScope: Each chat may edit only its own domain implementation and tests. Shared modules, cross-domain files, migration journal/snapshots, schema index, tracker and CI require a named single writer and documented handoff. No same-file parallel edits.
coordination.migrationIntegrator: Only L01 promotes numbered migrations, journal, snapshots and schema index, atomically from fresh main. Other lanes prepare domain-local change requests and tests; L01 registers in ordered batches. Never independently reserve the next migration number.
coordination.trackerWriter: Each chat may update its own claim, owned task acceptance and milestones in this one JSON file using a fresh blob SHA / expected head, preserving all other lanes. On any conflict re-read, merge only intended fields, validate, retry without force.
coordination.dependencyPolicy: Explicit tracker dependsOn gates remain binding. Domain producer owns cross-domain fixes; consumer requests a handoff. Independent verification is L10; global release/schema signoff requires L01 and L10 executed results.
coordination.handoffRequestContract: Use execution.sharedChangeRequests with {id,fromLane,toLane,paths,reason,status,requestedAt}; status REQUESTED/ACCEPTED/APPLIED/REJECTED. This is coordination metadata, not an accepted task or a second tracker. Do not edit another lane's code before ACCEPTED.
coordination.commitProtocol: Every cohesive commit must name Lane: LNN in message body; verify changed paths against lane ownership, rebase on fresh main before updating ref, never force. Tagged cross-lane integration requires an explicit handoff and the single designated writer.
testTiers: During change: fast affected static/type/unit tests

Global phase gate: full applicable typecheck/lint/build/browser/security plus release-only provider/recovery at RELEASE
coordination.progressRule: Counts derive from the done booleans in tasks and milestones; lane claim and request status do not imply engineering acceptance.

startupProcedure: Read AGENTS.md, docs/tracker.json (execution + tasks), and latest relevant source/code/test; do not read historical plans as current instruction.
Take a free designated lane L01-L10 and claim it with a unique sessionId using optimistic Git update; if occupied, pick another idle lane or ask the existing lane to hand off.
Read assigned unaccepted DB IDs and relevant phase milestones; choose highest-value dependency-ready finite real workflow.
Implement coherent code+registered migration via L01 if needed+real consumer+tests; run disposable DB acceptance and domain negatives.
Commit with Lane trailer, update ONLY owned accepted items and exact evidence in this same tracker by fresh-main optimistic merge, then freeze and move.
Before context ends, release or explicitly hand off lane claim; next chat reads canonical tracker not previous conversation prose.

globalPhaseRules.canonicalStageOrder: execution.globalPhases (DATABASE, API, UI, DESIGN, RELEASE) is the explicit five-stage roadmap in this same tracker; top-level phaseOrder/currentPhase stay the four historical certification buckets for compatibility, with DESIGN an independent sub-gate before RELEASE.
globalPhaseRules.statusDerivation: The only authoritative global certification flags and evidence are execution.globalPhaseCertificates; globalPhases contains scope and immutable acceptance contract, not copied done/status fields. globalPhaseRules.phasePromotion: Independent certification must only occur after all prerequisite stages are certified, all required scoped tasks/milestones pass, all relevant phaseGates and globalPhases.exitCriteria are satisfied with executed code-SHA evidence. globalPhaseRules.tenChatRule: All ten lanes can implement dependency-ready work in parallel in the active phase; a domain-local future-stage user journey is a useful implementation but not global certification. All lane claims/handoffs live in this same JSON.
globalPhaseRules.changes: Only user-authorized scope changes. Never silently drop an expected phase, required role/surface or test to raise completion percentage.
